replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: I have a complicated relationship with math. While I enjoyed biology and chemistry in school, math always felt more abstract and intimidating. I appreciate its importance in science, but it doesn't come naturally to me. My parents are both highly educated, so there's some pressure to excel, but I've learned to accept my limitations. I focus on practical applications rather than theoretical concepts.

replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, make sure it's in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / 2a. Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac) first - if it's positive, you get two real solutions; if zero, one solution; if negative, complex solutions. Plug the numbers into the formula carefully, doing the square root first, then the division. Check your answers by plugging them back into the original equation.

First, find the derivative f'(x) - this gives you the slope at any point. Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x - these are your stationary points. Then use the second derivative f''(x) to classify them: if f''(x) > 0, it's a minimum; if f''(x) < 0, it's a maximum; if f''(x) = 0, it could be an inflection point. Finally, plug the x-values back into the original f(x) to get the y-coordinates.
